title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 92-94): Grothendieck is working out when an automorphism Θ of a profinite fundamental groupoid lifts to a covering. The intended application is to give necessary conditions for an automorphism of π̂_1(X_{K̄}, I), with I ⊂ X(K) a set of rational base points, to come from an element of Γ = Gal(K̄/K).

Setting. Let 𝒞 be a connected groupoid (on the page 𝒞 or T) and 𝒞̃ → 𝒞 a covering, with 𝒞' ⊂ 𝒞̃ a connected component. Θ is an automorphism of 𝒞 fixing the object x_0. Write Π_0 = π_1(𝒞, x_0).

Fibre. The fibre E_0 = Ob 𝒞̃_{x_0} is a homogeneous Π_0-set. Choosing x'_0 ∈ E_0 identifies E_0 ≅ Π_0/Π'_0, where Π'_0 = Im(π_1(𝒞̃, x'_0) → π_1(𝒞, x_0)) is the stabilizer of x'_0. This is formula (47); the handwritten '47,' was misread as 'si'.

Lifting criterion. By the previous page, lifting Θ to Θ̃ on 𝒞̃ is equivalent to giving a Θ-semilinear bijection Θ̃_0 of E_0, i.e. Θ̃_0(g·x') = Θ(g)·Θ̃_0(x') (formula 46). Such a map is determined by x'_1 = Θ̃_0(x'_0). The constraint is that the stabilizer of x'_1 must equal Θ(Π'_0).
- If x'_1 = g·x'_0, its stabilizer is int(g)(Π'_0).
- So a lift exists iff Θ(Π'_0) is conjugate to Π'_0 in Π_0.
- The lifts are in bijection with the g satisfying int(g)(Π'_0) = Θ(Π'_0) (48), i.e. g ∈ Transp_{Π_0}(Π'_0, Θ(Π'_0)), taken modulo right multiplication by Π'_0.
- Hence the set of lifts is Transp_{Π_0}(Π'_0, Θ(Π'_0))/Π'_0 (49). This is a right-homogeneous space under N_{Π_0}(Π'_0)/Π'_0, the deck group of the connected cover.

Marginal remarks.
- Existence depends only on the outer class of Θ acting on Π_0, but the actual set of lifts depends on more than the outer action.
- One must also take care that lifts to 𝒞̃ preserve the chosen connected component 𝒞'.

Application. For 𝒞 = π̂_1(X_{K̄}, I) and 𝒞' = π̂_1(X'_{K̄}, I'), with X' → X finite étale and I' over I, liftability of Θ is 'une condition algébrique des plus simples': a conjugacy condition on open subgroups.

Next page. This feeds the necessary conditions for Θ to come from Γ:
- (a) Θ lifts to every finite étale cover X' defined over K, with the lift acting trivially on the rational points of I'.
- (b) For every map X' → Y to a hyperbolic curve over K, the image of π̂_1(X') → π̂_1(Y) is stable under the lift (or under Θ^ν at non-rational points).
These are early I/OM-type ('functoriality') constraints on the Galois image in Out(π̂_1).
errors: Marginal note says Π'_0 acts on the right on the transporter 'via g ↦ gα pour α ∈ Π_0'; it should read α ∈ Π'_0 (or, for transitivity on the quotient, the normalizer N_{Π_0}(Π'_0)). This is a slip of the pen.
The criterion is stated for a single automorphism Θ. For a group action of Θ one would also need the lifts to compose coherently (a cocycle/obstruction issue), which is not addressed here.
Lifts of Θ to 𝒞̃ preserve the chosen connected component 𝒞' only if they stabilise it. Grothendieck flags this himself in the 'Bien noter' margin note, so it is acknowledged rather than an error.

ideas.what: Lifting an automorphism Θ of a groupoid/group to a covering: a lift exists iff Θ(Π'_0) is conjugate to Π'_0; lifts form Transp_{Π_0}(Π'_0, Θ(Π'_0))/Π'_0
ideas.modern_name: Lifting criterion for automorphisms to covering spaces (Galois-category version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical covering space theory (Poincaré, Reidemeister); Grothendieck SGA1 for the Galois-category form
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1 Exp. V (Galois categories, fibre functors)

ideas.what: The existence condition depends only on the outer action of Θ, while the set of lifts depends on the actual automorphism
ideas.modern_name: Outer vs. genuine actions; torsor of lifts under N(Π'_0)/Π'_0

ideas.what: Applying the criterion to π̂_1(X_{K̄}, I) with rational base points, to derive necessary conditions (on the next page) for an automorphism to come from Gal(K̄/K): liftability to all K-defined covers, and stability of images of π_1 under maps to hyperbolic curves
ideas.modern_name: Characterisation of the Galois image in Out(π̂_1) via geometric functoriality (Ihara / Oda–Matsumoto 'I/OM')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Oda–Matsumoto conjecture (~1990); Pop (proof of variants)
ideas.where_published: The spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (Galois as automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower), but not this precise form

missed.claim: This page sets up the formalism that, on the next page, yields I/OM-type necessary conditions for an outer automorphism of π̂_1 of a curve with rational base points to be Galois. The conditions are liftability to every K-defined finite étale cover, plus preservation of images of π_1 under morphisms to hyperbolic curves. This anticipates by about a decade the Oda–Matsumoto / Ihara question and Pop's I/OM results; the published history credits Ihara, Oda–Matsumoto and Pop.
missed.quote: la condition qu'une action de 𝒞 Θ se remonte en une action de 𝒞' est une condition algébrique des plus simples
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point. The page itself is routine covering theory, but it is the technical basis of Grothendieck's early 'functoriality' characterisation of the Galois image, which he does not seem to have published in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is the standard lifting criterion for automorphisms to coverings, expressed via transporters. Its only interest is as preparation for the next page's I/OM-like conditions, which are historically noteworthy but not on this page.
transcription_corrections: The line 'si [?], E_0 ≃ Π_0/Π'_0' should be '(47) E_0 ≃ π_0/π'_0': the handwritten '47,' was misread as '§7'/'si'.
'on sait que ⊄ [?]' is 'on sait que', followed by a reference/insertion mark, not a mathematical symbol; the same mark recurs before 'Ainsi … dans le cas'.
Margin 'α ∈ Π_0' is written as such but should mathematically be α ∈ Π'_0.
Margin note reads approximately: 'cette condition ne dépend que de l'action ext. définie par Θ sur π_0 — mais les façons de remonter Θ en Θ̃_0 en dépendent' (ext. = extérieure).
In 'π̂_1(X_K, I)' and 'π̂_1(X'_K, I')' the subscript should be K̄ (geometric fibre), consistent with I ⊂ X_K being rational points.
The groupoid is denoted with the same letter as T on the previous page; '𝒞' vs 'T' is a transcription inconsistency.
